title: Horizon-Restricted Leading Soft QED as Open Quantum System
abstract: I formulate black-hole-horizon-induced decoherence of charged branch codes as the leading-soft QED restricted to an exterior algebra, formulated as an open quantum system. The fixed-history Feynman--Vernon identity ${\cal F}[J,J]=1$ remains exact. Decoherence enters through the unequal-history influence factor that survives exterior monitoring and belongs to the complementary horizon output. In the coherent eikonal regime, I derive the completely positive Schur channel $({\cal E}_H^{(0)}ρ)_{ab}=\langleΦ_b^{H,(0)}|Φ_a^{H,(0)}\rangle \, ρ_{ab}$. The leading soft input is the eikonal factor, projected onto the horizon radiative algebra. The channel yields Gram-positivity constraints, an exterior quantum-eraser bound, finite-time non-Markovianity tests, soft/hard scaling criteria, and a charged-qutrit interferometer measuring a leading-soft Bargmann holonomy. The holonomy phase is the rephasing-invariant symplectic area of a triangle in horizon soft phase space. I show that its orientation, common-mode, triangulation, and completely positive determinant identities render falsifiable tests beyond pairwise two-path visibility.
summary: This theoretical paper models black-hole decoherence by treating the interaction as an open quantum system governed by leading-soft QED. It derives a specific Schur channel that quantifies how coherence is lost due to monitoring the horizon environment. The results yield new, testable constraints on quantum information processing in curved spacetime.
main_problem: The paper formulates black-hole-horizon-induced decoherence of charged branch codes within an open quantum system framework, treating the interaction as a leading-soft QED process.
main_result: It derives a completely positive Schur channel characterizing coherence loss due to horizon monitoring and establishes falsifiable tests for this decoherence beyond simple two-path visibility.
method: The analysis employs an Open Quantum System (OQS) approach, utilizing the fixed-history Feynman–Vernon identity and analyzing the system's evolution via a Schur multiplier derived from the horizon output algebra.
model_or_system: The model involves charged bodies near black hole horizons or Killing horizons, where decoherence is induced by coupling to an external, soft radiative environment. The formalism uses 'branch currents' ($J_\mu^a$) and defines the system via algebraic bipartitions of the radiation algebra.
key_observables: Gram-positivity constraints, exterior quantum-eraser bound, finite-time non-Markovianity tests, and a leading-soft Bargmann holonomy phase (symplectic area).
important_parameters: Black hole mass ($M$), charge ($q$), separation ($d$), time ($T$), and the soft/hard scaling criteria.

paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the OQS framework for horizon decoherence, deriving the Schur channel in the eikonal limit, and then applying this formalism to derive specific physical constraints like non-Markovianity tests and geometric invariants (holonomy).
why_interesting: This work bridges quantum information theory (Schur channels, coherence bounds) with fundamental aspects of general relativity and QED near horizons, providing novel diagnostics for gravitational decoherence.

The thick upper and lower hori- zontal segments represent the spacelike singularities r = 0. The diagonal line labelled H+ R is the future event horizon bounding the right exterior region occupied by Alice. The left exterior, the white-hole region, and most other labels are omitted because they are spectators for the open-system con- struction.
